source_zh: 从保管文件到理解历史
translation_en: From Keeping Documents to Understanding History

source_zh: ——我对档案员职业与档案的再认识
translation_en: Rethinking the Archival Profession and Archives

source_zh: 我最初并不理解，档案员为什么需要知道研究者正在思考什么。在我的印象中，这份工作接近manager：保管文件、安排阅览，按照使用者的需要调出材料。只要材料没有遗失、查找足够方便，工作似乎就已经完成。因此，读到“研究伙伴”时，我想到的首先是疑问：一个并不熟悉我的课题的人，能够怎样参与研究？如果档案员也解释材料，他们与历史学家的区别又在哪里？这些问题看似围绕职责，背后却有一个我没有察觉的前提：我把研究放在取得材料以后，把帮助我取得材料的工作放在研究以外。
translation_en: At first, I did not understand why archivists needed to know what researchers were thinking about. I saw their work as similar to a manager’s: keeping documents, arranging access, and retrieving materials according to users’ needs. As long as nothing was lost and materials were easy to find, the job seemed complete. So when I read the phrase “research partner,” my first response was a series of questions: How could someone unfamiliar with my topic take part in my research? If archivists also interpreted materials, how did their work differ from that of historians? These questions seemed to concern professional duties, but they rested on an assumption I had not noticed: I placed research after obtaining materials and treated the work that helped me obtain them as outside research.

source_zh: 第七至第十周的学习，使我逐渐看见这个前提的局限。我开始关心，材料为什么会以眼前的方式存在，又是谁使我有可能找到和理解它。随着这些问题展开，档案员在我眼中也有了更具体的面貌：他们需要研究馆藏的形成，判断记录之间的关系，并让不同的人能够接近这些关系。我对这一职业的认识，并非只是增加了几项职责，而是开始理解历史研究可以有不同的工作方式。档案员因而成为我思考历史研究者职业方向时，能够认真考虑的一种可能。
translation_en: The learning in Weeks 7–10 gradually showed me the limits of this assumption. I began to ask why materials existed in their present form and who made it possible for me to find and understand them. As these questions developed, I gained a clearer picture of archivists: they study how collections took shape, assess relationships between records, and help different people understand those relationships. My changing view of the profession involved more than adding a few duties to a list. I began to understand that historical research can take different forms. Archival work therefore became a career path I could seriously consider when thinking about the options open to historical researchers.

source_zh: 这一变化又带出第二个问题：如果理解材料本来就是工作的一部分，他们究竟需要理解怎样的材料？传单、衣着、住所中的记忆，以及被赋予公共意义的原件，使“档案”这个我原以为熟悉的词变得不再简单。我需要重新说明什么能够成为档案，以及这样认定的理由。不过，我想先从自己的职业疑问出发。正是在尝试理解档案员为什么需要研究、又需要研究到什么程度时，我才逐渐发现，对这个职业的理解与对档案的理解始终联系在一起。
translation_en: This change led to a second question: if understanding materials is already part of the job, what kinds of materials do archivists need to understand? Leaflets, clothing, memories connected to homes, and original documents given public significance made “archives,” a term I thought I knew, less straightforward. I needed to reconsider what could count as archives and why. But I want to begin with my questions about the profession. It was while trying to understand why archivists needed to do research, and how much research their work required, that I gradually saw how closely an understanding of the profession was connected to an understanding of archives.

source_zh: 一、保管工作中的判断
translation_en: 1. Judgment in Preservation

source_zh: 我先前评价档案员的方式，主要围绕使用者能否顺利取得材料。这样的期待当然有实际理由，但它只能看见工作的结果。文件被调到面前之前，需要有人说明它属于什么、与什么相关，以及为什么会保存在这里。如果这些问题都已经有了答案，查找容易被看成执行程序；问题在于，答案并不会自然附在每份文件上。档案员必须作出理解，程序才有可以依循的内容。这使我开始把保管和查找中的判断当作问题，而不只是把它们当作研究的准备。
translation_en: I used to assess archivists mainly by whether users could obtain materials smoothly. This expectation had practical reasons, but it revealed only the results of their work. Before a document reaches a reader, someone needs to explain where it belongs, what it relates to, and why it is kept there. If these questions already have answers, finding materials can look like following a procedure. The problem is that the answers do not come attached to every document. The procedures themselves depend on archivists’ understanding of the materials. This led me to examine the judgments involved in keeping and finding records, rather than treating them only as preparation for research.

source_zh: 我对“档案员是作者”的第一反应，也带着类似的局限。作者在我心中首先意味着写作，因而这个说法似乎是在把属于历史学家的创造性赋予另一种职业。但契据簿让我看到，一部编纂物的整体形态，已经包含对原有文字的选择和安排。哪些内容被抄入、怎样安排、后来怎样续补，会影响这部材料能够讲述什么，也可能参与当时的产权主张。Geary使我注意的，因而不是档案员是否像历史学家一样写出了故事，而是编纂已经建立了后来研究者使用的关系。
translation_en: My first response to “archivists as authors” reflected a similar limitation. To me, being an author primarily meant writing, so the phrase seemed to give another profession a form of creativity I associated with historians. But cartularies showed me that the overall form of a compilation already involved selecting and arranging existing texts. What was copied, how it was arranged, and how it was later supplemented could affect what the material could tell us. It could also contribute to property claims at the time. What Geary drew my attention to was therefore not whether archivists wrote stories as historians did, but how compilation had already established relationships that later researchers would use.

source_zh: 不过，仅仅接受“作者”这个称呼，我仍没有真正理解工作。契据簿背后有主教的授权、抄写者的改写和后人的补充，不能只靠一个姓名说明它怎样形成。对我更有帮助的追问是，这些人分别做了什么，什么安排被保留下来，又有哪些联系是后来才出现的。这样看，档案员的研究能力就在具体辨认之中：需要把材料的形成过程解释清楚，而不是笼统地宣称自己也参与了历史生产。我原来觉得抽象的职业作用，才在这些问题中变得可以认识。
translation_en: However, simply accepting the label “author” did not mean I understood the work. Behind a cartulary were a bishop’s authorization, a scribe’s revisions, and later additions. A single name could not explain how it took shape. I found it more useful to ask what each person did, which arrangements survived, and which connections appeared later. From this perspective, archivists’ research skills lay in making these specific distinctions. They needed to explain how materials were formed, rather than broadly claiming to participate in the production of history. A professional role I had found abstract became easier to understand through these questions.

source_zh: 还有一些判断，比编纂和整理发生得更早。我起初习惯在已有材料中选择适合自己问题的部分，较少从保存者的角度思考，一批记录为什么值得留下。读Cook时，这个顺序被倒了过来：今天的选择，会影响尚未出现的人能够研究什么。判断保存价值，因而需要理解记录由什么活动产生，保存了怎样的社会联系。它不能只等研究者提出需要以后再作回应，因为那时有些材料可能早已不在。档案员面对的研究问题，在这里与我的专题兴趣拉开了距离。
translation_en: Some judgments take place even before compilation and arrangement. I was initially used to selecting useful parts of existing materials for my own questions. I gave less thought to why a body of records was worth preserving from the keeper’s perspective. Reading Cook reversed this order: choices made today affect what future researchers will be able to study. Assessing preservation value therefore requires understanding the activities that produced records and the social relationships they preserve. It cannot simply wait for researchers to express a need, because some materials may already be gone by then. The research questions archivists face thus differ from my own topic interests.

source_zh: 这种距离也解释了我为什么不能把鉴定想成替未来猜选题。未来的人可能关心今天不受重视的事情，而我也不能因为一份记录暂时无用于自己的问题，就判断它没有保存意义。考察记录产生的职能和关系，为我提供了另一个思考方向：先理解某种活动留下了什么，再判断取舍会让我们失去怎样的认识机会。对未来负责并不要求预见全部未来，却要求认识今天正在选择的对象。我开始理解，这种工作需要历史眼光，也有不同于完成一篇专题论文的要求。
translation_en: This difference also explains why I cannot think of appraisal as guessing future research topics. People in the future may care about things that receive little attention today. Nor can I decide that a record has no preservation value simply because it is not currently useful to my question. Examining the functions and relationships that produced records offered another way to think: first understand what an activity left behind, then consider which opportunities for understanding might be lost through selection. Responsibility to the future does not require foreseeing the whole future. It does require understanding the objects of today’s choices. I began to see why this work needed a historical perspective and involved demands different from those of completing a paper on a particular topic.

source_zh: 整理同样包含我原来没有充分看见的判断。我曾期待，简明统一的编码能够减少查找困难，因此较容易把目录看成可以改良的工具。问题是，同一份材料可能涉及不同的人与活动，把它放在一个名称之下，已经突出了一种关系。Yakel关于档案再现的讨论，使我重新考虑自己的期待。标准仍然有用，但了解标准，还应包括知道它使什么容易被看见。否则，目录越方便，我越可能忘记查找路径也是被人组织出来的。
translation_en: Arrangement also involves judgments I had not fully recognized. I once hoped that simple, consistent codes would make materials easier to find, so I tended to view catalogs as tools that could be improved. Yet a single item may concern different people and activities. Placing it under one name already highlights a particular relationship. Yakel’s discussion of archival representation made me reconsider my expectation. Standards remain useful, but understanding a standard should also mean knowing what it makes easier to see. Otherwise, the more convenient a catalog becomes, the more easily I may forget that someone organized the routes through which I search.

source_zh: 数字界面尤其容易使这部分劳动隐去。输入关键词、看到结果，似乎是使用者与材料直接相遇；但使用的名称和被描述的内容，都依赖先前的理解。如果没有找到，我需要区分是未曾记录、未被保存、尚未开放，还是自己的词汇与目录没有相接。档案员能够帮助辨认这些差别，靠的就不仅是熟悉文件号码。对我而言，认识这种帮助的价值，也意味着改变提问方式：与其只要求一个检索结果，不如询问我正通过怎样的路径接近材料。
translation_en: Digital interfaces can make this work especially difficult to see. Entering keywords and receiving results can seem like a direct encounter between a user and materials. But the names used and the content described both depend on earlier understandings. If I find nothing, I need to distinguish between something never recorded, something not preserved, something not yet accessible, and a mismatch between my vocabulary and the catalog. Helping me identify these differences requires more than knowing file numbers. Recognizing the value of this help also changes how I ask questions: rather than only requesting a search result, I can ask about the route through which I am approaching the materials.

source_zh: 这些问题使我逐渐放下了管理与研究之间过于明确的界线。材料需要被妥善保管，阅览也需要安排；但支撑这些工作的是对材料来历和关系的持续理解。我以前把研究想象成在材料中得出某个结论，现在开始看到，使材料能够被理解，也可以成为需要长期投入的工作。这并没有让我认定档案员与历史学家已经没有区别，反而使那个区别更值得追问：如果两者都需要判断，他们分别需要知道什么，又应当怎样一起工作？
translation_en: These questions gradually made me reconsider the sharp boundary I had drawn between management and research. Materials need proper care, and access needs to be arranged, but these tasks rest on a continuing understanding of the materials’ origins and relationships. I used to imagine research as reaching a conclusion from materials. I now began to see that making materials understandable could itself require sustained work. This did not convince me that archivists and historians were no longer distinct. Instead, it made the distinction more worth examining: if both need to make judgments, what does each need to know, and how should they work together?

source_zh: 二、从要求理解到学习合作
translation_en: 2. From Expecting Others to Understand to Learning to Work Together

source_zh: 承认档案员需要理解材料以后，我很快遇到了另一个困难：理解究竟要达到什么程度？我起初想到的办法是培训，让档案员更熟悉研究问题，减少他们与历史学家的距离。这个办法似乎直接，却仍以研究者为中心：仿佛应当由对方补上知识，合作才可能发生。我没有同时追问，自己是否理解档案的形成制度，是否知道目录语言为什么与我的提问不同。后来，我才逐渐意识到，要求别人更了解我，也可能使我忽略自己需要学习的部分。
translation_en: Once I accepted that archivists needed to understand materials, I soon encountered another difficulty: how much understanding was enough? My initial answer was training that would make archivists more familiar with research questions and bring them closer to historians. This seemed straightforward, but it remained centered on the researcher, as though the other person needed to fill a knowledge gap before cooperation could begin. I did not also ask whether I understood the institutional processes that produced records or why catalog language differed from my questions. I gradually realized that expecting others to understand me better could also lead me to overlook what I needed to learn.

source_zh: 核医学的例子使这个困难有了一个具体出口。Marquis并不熟悉研究者的领域，却通过提问，把问题与馆藏中的物理学研究联系起来。如果合作必须等到双方已经掌握相同知识，这种联系很难出现。陌生在这里并非只能构成障碍，也能让人解释自己原本习以为常的问题。我由此开始区分两种理解：掌握一个领域的全部内容，与知道怎样追问、怎样把问题放回材料之间的关系，并不是同一件事。后者已经可能使咨询对研究产生作用。
translation_en: The example of nuclear medicine offered a concrete way through this difficulty. Marquis was unfamiliar with the researcher’s field, yet was able to connect the topic to research in physics represented in the collection by asking questions. If cooperation had to wait until both sides possessed the same knowledge, this connection would have been difficult to make. Unfamiliarity did not only create an obstacle. It could also prompt people to explain questions they otherwise took for granted. I began to distinguish between two kinds of understanding: knowing all the content of a field and knowing how to ask questions and relate a problem to connections between materials. The latter could already make reference work useful to research.

source_zh: 这样看，我原来设想的培训方向就显得不够完整。馆藏涉及许多领域，档案员不可能预先准备好所有问题；而研究者即使熟悉自己的专题，也未必知道材料怎样被组织。双方的知识并不需要完全重合。档案员可以帮助我认识馆藏，我则需要把提问说明到足以交流的程度，并判断一条建议是否适用。合作所要求的学习是双向的：我不能只把对方的知识看作服务自己的资源，也需要认真理解这种知识从哪里来、能够回答什么。
translation_en: Seen this way, my original idea of training was incomplete. Collections cover many fields, and archivists cannot prepare for every question in advance. Researchers may know their own topics well without knowing how materials are organized. Their knowledge need not overlap completely. Archivists can help me understand a collection, while I need to explain my question clearly enough for discussion and judge whether a suggestion applies. The learning required for cooperation goes both ways. I cannot treat the other person’s knowledge only as a resource for my needs. I also need to understand where that knowledge comes from and what it can answer.

source_zh: 我对“为什么档案员要解释证据价值”的疑问，也在这里发生了变化。我曾把解释想得过重，仿佛一旦介入，就需要替文件中的说法担保。现在，我更愿意从材料如何形成、保存和改动来理解这种帮助。比如，在Bartlett讨论的钟人杰案中，一份供词即使能够完整留下，也不说明被记录者按自己的方式说出了经历。地方官员避免失察责任的需要，就与供词的说法有关。认识这种关系，有助于提出问题，却仍不能直接确定起义是否早有预谋。
translation_en: My question about why archivists should explain evidential value also changed. I had made the task of interpretation too demanding in my mind, as though anyone who took part had to guarantee what a document said. I now prefer to understand this help through how materials were created, preserved, and altered. For example, in the Zhong Renjie case discussed by Bartlett, the complete survival of a confession does not mean that the person recorded described his experiences in his own way. Local officials’ need to avoid blame for failing to detect the rebellion was connected to what the confession said. Recognizing this relationship helps us raise questions, but it still does not establish directly whether the uprising had been planned long in advance.

source_zh: 这个例子使我更能说明合作中的责任。了解记录制度的人，可以指出一份材料需要放在哪些关系中阅读；使用它提出历史解释的人，则还要说明这些关系怎样支持自己的判断。二者相互依赖，却没有谁因此能替另一个人完成全部工作。档案员解释材料来历，并不是越过职责替我作结论；我保留最后的判断，也不意味着先前的说明无关紧要。我原先担心的职业重叠，因而逐渐转变为一个更具体的问题：如何使不同的理解能够相互检验。
translation_en: This example helped me explain the responsibilities involved in cooperation. Someone who understands the system of record creation can identify the relationships within which a source needs to be read. Someone who uses it to offer a historical interpretation must still explain how those relationships support the argument. The two depend on each other, but neither can do all the other’s work. Explaining a source’s origins does not mean that an archivist is stepping beyond their role and reaching conclusions for me. My responsibility for the final judgment does not make that earlier explanation unimportant. My initial concern about overlapping professions gradually became a more specific question: how can different understandings be tested against each other?

source_zh: 我仍然在意研究者为什么愿意分享选题。一个尚未成熟的问题，未必容易向别人说明；研究者也可能不想交出全部设想。因此，伙伴关系不能只靠要求开放来建立。交流可以从一个目录名称、一组材料的来源，或一次具体的查找困难开始，再由双方决定是否继续。我对合作的期待因而比起初更有限，也更实际：愿意听取建议，不等于承诺接受建议；获得帮助，也不应以放弃控制研究计划为条件。承认专业能力与尊重自愿，可以同时存在。
translation_en: I still care about why researchers would be willing to share their topics. An unfinished question may be difficult to explain, and researchers may not want to reveal all their plans. Partnership cannot therefore be built simply by demanding openness. An exchange can begin with a catalog term, the origins of a group of materials, or a specific search problem. Both sides can then decide whether to continue. My expectations of cooperation have become more limited but also more practical: willingness to hear advice is not a promise to accept it, and receiving help should not require giving up control of a research plan. Recognition of professional expertise and respect for voluntary participation can coexist.

source_zh: 理解的差异也不一定能够通过沟通完全消除。档案员想到的馆藏关联，可能与我的问题不相同，有时会引出新的方向，有时则需要搁置。如果把每次差异都看作服务失败，我仍然只在要求对方猜中自己的需要。现在我更愿意把建议看成有根据、也可以被讨论的判断，询问它为什么成立，再说明自己为何采纳或不采纳。合作的价值不必体现为两个人最终说同样的话，也可能体现为，我因此更清楚地知道自己的问题究竟需要什么材料。
translation_en: Differences in understanding cannot necessarily be removed through communication. A connection an archivist sees within a collection may differ from my question. It may open a new direction, or it may need to be set aside. If I treat every difference as a failure of service, I am still asking the other person to guess my needs correctly. I now prefer to regard a suggestion as a judgment that has reasons and can be discussed. I can ask why it makes sense and then explain why I accept or reject it. Cooperation need not result in two people saying the same thing. Its value may instead lie in helping me understand more clearly what materials my question actually requires.

source_zh: 回看这些疑问，我开始认识自己的研究依赖怎样的知识。读到一份材料的内容时，我还需要理解它为什么被保存在这里，为什么以这种方式被找到。这些原来被我放在研究外围的问题，现在已经进入我的学习之中。我也因此更能理解，一位能够提出这些问题、长期研究并向他人说明的人，为什么可以被看作研究伙伴。接下来的问题，则是怎样把这种认识落实到对一份职业的理解。
translation_en: Looking back at these questions, I began to recognize the kinds of knowledge my research depended on. When I read the content of a source, I also needed to understand why it was preserved there and why it could be found in that way. Questions I once placed at the edge of research have now become part of my learning. I can therefore better understand why someone who raises these questions, studies them over time, and explains them to others can be seen as a research partner. The next question is how to turn this recognition into an understanding of a profession.

source_zh: 三、作为职业的历史研究
translation_en: 3. Historical Research as a Profession

source_zh: 我对档案员的认识逐渐清楚以后，也开始重新考虑自己用什么标准辨认历史研究。提出问题、阅读史料、写成文章，是我最熟悉的研究方式；档案工作则让我看见，研究还可以体现为把一批材料的来历、结构和相互关系说明清楚。这样的认识会进入馆藏的选择、目录的描述和面向使用者的说明之中。它未必以一篇专题论文出现，却可能影响许多不同的论文如何展开。我开始理解，历史训练所形成的能力，可以通过这种方式转化为持续的职业工作。
translation_en: As my understanding of archivists became clearer, I also began to reconsider what I counted as historical research. Asking questions, reading sources, and writing papers were the forms of research I knew best. Archival work showed me that research could also take the form of explaining the origins, structure, and relationships of a body of materials. This knowledge enters collection selection, catalog descriptions, and explanations for users. It may not appear as a paper on a particular topic, but it can affect how many different papers develop. I began to understand how the skills gained through historical training could become a sustained form of professional work.

source_zh: 这也让我更认真地看待自己对manager的最初印象。我看到的管理事务是真实的，只是没有看见其中需要的知识。一份材料能否与另一份一并查阅，为什么分属不同的类别，某些内容为何暂时不能使用，都可能需要了解它们的形成和保存经历。有效地回答这些问题，需要将制度、人物与具体活动联系起来。我的职业认识之所以局限，不是因为留意了日常事务，而是因为把事务想成了没有研究内容的执行。我现在愿意花更多力气理解，判断是怎样进入日常工作的。
translation_en: This also made me take my initial image of archivists as managers more seriously. The administrative tasks I saw were real; I simply had not recognized the knowledge they required. Whether one item should be consulted alongside another, why they belong to different categories, and why certain content is temporarily unavailable may all require knowledge of how the materials were created and preserved. Answering these questions effectively requires connecting institutions, people, and specific activities. My view of the profession was limited not because I noticed everyday tasks, but because I imagined them as routine tasks with no research involved. I now want to make more effort to understand how judgment enters daily work.

source_zh: 不过，看见判断以后，我也不能把档案员想成只要凭个人见识就能决定一切的人。读到违抗销毁命令而保存禁书的选择时，我愿意赞赏其中对记忆的坚持。但个人能够留下什么，还与他所处的位置、制度要求及监督条件有关。Bartlett留下的这个问题，使职业的能动性对我不再只是勇气或信念。我既需要注意个人作了怎样的选择，也需要理解他为什么有机会这样选择。对历史关系的研究，因而也包括认识自己工作条件的限制。
translation_en: Yet recognizing judgment does not mean imagining that archivists can decide everything through personal insight alone. When I read about the choice to preserve banned books against an order to destroy them, I valued the commitment to memory. But what someone could preserve also depended on their position, institutional requirements, and conditions of supervision. This question in Bartlett’s discussion made me see that an archivist’s ability to act was not simply a matter of courage or conviction. I needed to notice both the choice a person made and why they had the opportunity to make it. Studying historical relationships therefore also involves understanding the limits of one’s working conditions.

source_zh: 同样，承认档案员需要专业判断，并没有消除我对判断依据的疑问。保存若要体现社会价值，谁来说明什么对社会有价值？一个群体的代表人物，是否已经表达了其中所有人的保存愿望？在《Activist Archives》中，资深行动者能够凭借资源取得权威，不同群体后来又争夺“98一代”的代表资格。这使我更具体地理解Cook提出的责任：面对保存对象，需要研究哪些人的说法更容易出现，而不能把容易取得的版本直接当作共同意见。
translation_en: Similarly, recognizing the need for professional judgment has not removed my questions about its basis. If preservation is to reflect social value, who decides what has value for society? Has a group’s representative already expressed everyone’s wishes about preservation? In Activist Archives, senior activists gain authority through their resources, while different groups later compete to represent the “’98 generation.” This made Cook’s account of responsibility more concrete for me: when considering materials for preservation, we need to study whose accounts are more likely to appear, rather than treating the most accessible version as a shared view.

source_zh: 这个疑问并没有使我退回到希望档案员只按程序做事的立场。程序同样依赖判断，回避个人责任也不能使选择消失。我更愿意期待，专业者能够说明自己的理解依据什么，在作出取舍时考虑了哪些关系，也承认还有什么没有充分掌握。能够交代理由、听取其他认识，正是我现在重视的能力。历史训练可以支持这种能力，但它也要求学习具体档案业务。把档案员视为职业方向，因而需要认识专业要求，而不能只因为同样面对过去，就以为两种工作能够直接互换。
translation_en: This question has not taken me back to wishing that archivists would only follow procedures. Procedures also depend on judgment, and avoiding personal responsibility does not remove selection. I would rather expect professionals to explain the basis of their understanding, the relationships they considered when making choices, and what they have not yet fully understood. Giving reasons and listening to other views are skills I now value. Historical training can support these skills, but specific archival practices also need to be learned. Considering archival work as a career therefore requires understanding its professional demands. The two jobs cannot simply be treated as interchangeable because both concern the past.

source_zh: 我也重新理解了“为别人提供研究条件”的意义。若把研究成果只看成某位作者最后提出的解释，鉴定和描述容易成为完成解释之前的帮助；但一批材料的组织，可能在不同时间支持不同的问题。档案员需要理解眼前的使用者，同时为不熟悉的提问留下余地。我以前在一项研究中寻找有用材料，现在尝试换到另一个位置，思考怎样让一批材料可以面对多项研究。这个位置的变化，比给档案员增加“研究者”称号，更能帮助我认识工作的内容。
translation_en: I also reconsidered what it means to “provide the conditions for others to do research.” If a research outcome is understood only as an author’s final interpretation, appraisal and description can appear to be assistance offered before that interpretation is completed. Yet the organization of a collection may support different questions at different times. Archivists need to understand present users while leaving room for unfamiliar questions. I used to look for useful materials within a particular study. I am now trying to adopt another perspective and ask how a collection can support multiple studies. This shift in perspective helps me understand the work more than simply giving archivists the title of “researcher.”

source_zh: 所以，这几周我逐渐看到的职业可能，包含一种与自己原来想象不同的研究生活：长期接触材料，持续调整对其关系的理解，再把认识说明给有不同需要的人。吸引我注意的，是这种工作同时需要独立判断与沟通，也需要把个人兴趣放在更广泛的使用需求中考虑。我仍有许多业务知识需要学习，但已经能够理解，历史研究者为什么可以在这个方向继续运用和发展自己的训练。我对档案员的认识，也从使用者期待怎样获得服务，转向这份工作本身需要怎样的思考。
translation_en: The career possibility I gradually came to see in these weeks therefore involved a research life different from the one I had imagined: sustained work with materials, continuing revision of how their relationships are understood, and explanation of that understanding to people with different needs. What drew my attention was the combination of independent judgment and communication, along with the need to consider personal interests in relation to wider uses. I still have much to learn about archival practice, but I can now understand why historical researchers might continue to use and develop their training in this field. My view has shifted from the service a user expects to the thinking the work itself requires.

source_zh: 到这里，我原来的疑问并没有结束，而是换了一种形式。既然档案员需要理解记录的关系、参与判断其价值，我就不能再把他们面对的“档案”当作已经确定的对象。我们讨论了保存与描述，却还没有充分说明，究竟什么应当被保存和描述。早先阅读行动者材料时，纸张、衣着、影像与生活空间就让我感到边界不清。现在，我愿意把这个困惑重新提出：什么是档案？它既关系材料的称呼，也关系这份职业究竟研究和照顾怎样的对象。
translation_en: My original questions have not ended at this point; they have taken another form. If archivists need to understand relationships between records and help judge their value, I cannot treat the “archives” they work with as objects whose status is already settled. We have considered preservation and description, but have not fully explained what should be preserved and described. In my earlier reading about activists’ materials, paper, clothing, images, and living spaces had already made these boundaries unclear to me. I now want to raise that question again: what are archives? It concerns both what we call materials and what this profession studies and cares for.

source_zh: 四、从文件清单到记录关系
translation_en: 4. From Document Lists to Records and Their Relationships

source_zh: 如果按照我原来最容易想到的例子回答，档案首先是一批留下来的文件。它们有可以阅读的内容，进入某个保存场所，再等待研究者利用。这种理解能够说明一些材料，却很难解释我在行动者生活中遇到的记录。它们可能在搬迁中失散，在传递中被复制，也可能被要求销毁。若只用是否已经妥善保管来确认档案，许多材料在进入研究以前的作用就会被略去。我因而开始怀疑，自己的定义是否过于依赖后来使用者能够看见的状态。
translation_en: If I answered through the examples that used to come most readily to mind, archives would first mean a body of surviving documents. They contain readable information, enter a place of preservation, and then wait for researchers to use them. This understanding explains some materials, but it struggles to account for the records I encountered in activists’ lives. They might be scattered during moves, copied as they circulated, or ordered to be destroyed. If I recognized archives only by whether they were already properly preserved, I would overlook much of what the materials did before they entered research. I therefore began to wonder whether my definition depended too heavily on the condition in which later users could see them.

source_zh: 纸张最先使这个问题具体起来。我起初认为，文字提供信息，纸本身则是一件年代遗物；但诗歌与庭审传单参与争取支持，被丢弃的传单又因Wilson的拾取获得继续留存的机会。两种情境都涉及纸张，却在做不同的事情：它能够联系支持者，也能在一次保存选择之后成为后来者使用的材料。阅读这些经历时，我开始把复印、传递和捡拾放进对记录的理解，而不再只看它上面写了什么。（Lee，第25—30、57—59页）
translation_en: Paper first made this question concrete. I initially thought that words provided information while the paper itself was a relic of an earlier time. Yet poems and trial leaflets helped seek support, while discarded leaflets gained another chance to survive when Wilson picked them up. Both situations involved paper, but it was doing different things: connecting supporters and, after a decision to preserve it, becoming material for later users. Reading these experiences, I began to include copying, circulation, and collection in my understanding of records, rather than looking only at what was written on them.

source_zh: 这也使我放下了一个不自觉的期待：记录似乎总应当为了留下历史而产生。很多材料首先需要在当下起作用，后来才在新的问题中成为研究对象。档案因此可能具有不同的时间关系：它曾参与一次活动，今天又帮助别人认识那次活动；两种用途不必相同。对我而言，这比单纯把材料种类扩展到文字之外更有帮助。我需要说明的，是同一痕迹怎样进入不同的关系，以及后来的保存为什么没有把先前的用途完全抹去。
translation_en: This also helped me let go of an expectation I had not noticed: records seemed always to be created in order to preserve history. Many materials first needed to serve a purpose in the present and only later became research objects through new questions. Archives can therefore connect different times: a record once took part in an activity and now helps others understand that activity. The two uses need not be the same. I find this more useful than simply expanding the range of materials beyond writing. What I need to explain is how the same trace enters different relationships, and why later preservation has not completely erased its earlier uses.

source_zh: “家”的讨论又让我难以只按物品来划定档案。行动者的临时住所、组织总部和行动据点，同时承担休息、交往与保管材料的功能。Roni能指出旧据点房间的用途，也记得失火时未能救出文件的遗憾。住所并非只是文件之外的背景；谁能够提供空间，谁维持共同生活，会影响记录是否可能集中和延续。但我也不想因此直接把整所住所都当成档案。更准确的理解是，文件的来历包括这些生活关系，阅读文件时需要使它们重新可见。（Lee，第168—170页）
translation_en: The discussion of “home” also made it difficult for me to define archives only through objects. Activists’ temporary homes, organizational headquarters, and bases for action served as spaces for rest, interaction, and keeping materials. Roni could identify how the rooms in a former base had been used and remembered the regret of being unable to save documents from a fire. Housing was more than background outside the documents. Who could provide space and who sustained communal life affected whether records could be gathered and kept. But I do not want to treat the entire house as an archive on that basis. A more accurate understanding is that the documents’ origins include these living relationships, which need to be made visible again when the documents are read.

source_zh: 我曾希望知道记录应该存放在哪里，现在则会多问一步：某个地方为什么能够使记录留下？档案馆当然可以提供保存条件，共同生活中的空间也可能暂时承担这种作用。它们的条件与稳定程度并不相同，却都提醒我，材料的存续依赖人的劳动。这样理解以后，“什么是档案”就不只是辨认某类物品的外观，还需要解释物品与活动、保存者之间的联系。制度性馆藏与行动者的零散材料，也因此可以被比较，而不必先被视为完全分离的世界。
translation_en: I once wanted to know where records should be kept. I now ask an additional question: why could a particular place allow records to survive? An archival repository can provide conditions for preservation, and a shared living space may temporarily serve that purpose too. Their conditions and stability differ, but both remind me that the survival of materials depends on people’s work. Seen this way, “what are archives?” is not only a question of recognizing the appearance of certain objects. It also requires explaining connections between objects, activities, and keepers. Institutional collections and activists’ scattered materials can therefore be compared without first being treated as entirely separate worlds.

source_zh: 影像使记录关系的问题更加明显。学生为记者镜头重新列队宣誓时，学生的自我呈现、记者的取景与预想中的观众，都参与了画面的形成。我可以据此研究集体形象怎样被制作，却需要区分这一场景与原先的示威。这里令我在意的，并不只是影像有多少真实性，而是它究竟记录了怎样的活动。如果忽略形成方式，一张可以研究的影像也可能被误认为另一件事的直接记录。把它认作档案，还需要保留使这种区分成为可能的说明。（Lee，第181—182页）
translation_en: Images make these relationships clearer. When students lined up again to make a pledge for a journalist’s camera, their self-presentation, the journalist’s framing, and the imagined audience all helped produce the image. I can use it to study how a collective image was made, but I need to distinguish this scene from the original demonstration. What matters to me here is not only how truthful an image is, but what activity it actually records. If its production is ignored, an image worth studying may be mistaken for a direct record of something else. Recognizing it as archival material also requires keeping the contextual information that makes this distinction possible.

source_zh: 课堂上的新加坡石，以及我联想到的河流声音，把这个问题继续推向文字和图片以外。我愿意承认这些对象能够帮助认识过去，却仍需问，留下的究竟是什么，凭什么能够与某种经历相联系。声音可以被录下，物品可以被保留，但后来的读者还需要知道记录怎样形成、哪些关系值得注意。这使我对档案边界的态度有所变化：我不再急于排除不熟悉的形式，也不满足于只说它们承载了记忆，而是希望把能够研究它们的依据说得更清楚。
translation_en: The Singapore Stone discussed in class and the river sounds it reminded me of took this question further beyond writing and pictures. I am willing to recognize that these objects can help us understand the past, but still need to ask what has survived and on what basis it can be connected to an experience. Sound can be recorded and objects can be kept, yet later readers still need to know how the record was made and which relationships matter. My attitude toward archival boundaries has therefore changed: I am less quick to exclude unfamiliar forms, but am also not satisfied with simply saying that they carry memory. I want to explain more clearly the basis on which they can be studied.

source_zh: 由此，我逐渐把“文件清单”式的理解，转向对记录关系的理解。档案可以有不同载体，也可能经过不同的保存路径；共同的问题是，它们怎样使某种活动在后来仍有被认识的可能。不过，走到这里仍有一个困难：如果一件物品承载了很多意义，是否就足以被称为档案？原件与复制品的疑问，迫使我继续考虑自己究竟重视什么。否则，我只是把定义从熟悉的文件扩大为一切有记忆价值的事物，仍未说明档案如何成立。
translation_en: I gradually moved from understanding archives as “lists of documents” toward understanding the relationships behind records. Archives can have different media and follow different paths of preservation. The shared question is how they allow an activity to remain open to later understanding. Yet a difficulty remains: if an object carries many meanings, is that enough for it to count as archival material? My questions about originals and copies forced me to keep considering what I actually valued. Otherwise, I would merely be expanding the definition from familiar documents to everything with a value for memory, without explaining why it counts as archival material.

source_zh: 五、档案的认定与意义
translation_en: 5. Identifying Archives and Understanding Their Meaning

source_zh: 我现在倾向于把档案理解为，在具体活动中形成或留下、又通过保存与说明使那些活动能够被重新认识的记录。这个理解首先把记录放回形成它的关系，也承认后来的人会参与选择和解释。它不是我已经掌握的一套完整定义，而是阅读后能够用来检查自己判断的办法：面对一种材料，我需要说明它与什么活动有关，这种联系怎样被留下，今天又凭借什么被认识。仅仅说它古老、重要或令人感动，还不足以回答这些问题。
translation_en: I now tend to understand archives as records formed or left through particular activities that, through preservation and description, allow those activities to be understood again. This understanding first places records back in the relationships that produced them. It also recognizes that later people take part in selection and interpretation. It is not a complete definition that I have already mastered, but a way of checking my judgments after these readings. When I encounter a material, I need to explain which activity it relates to, how that connection was preserved, and how it can be recognized today. Saying only that it is old, important, or moving is not enough to answer these questions.

source_zh: 但如果只强调信息，这个理解又可能变得过窄。我原来问，文字已经复制传播，为什么还需要原件？问题背后是把档案的作用主要理解为向研究者提供内容。一旦内容已有副本，原件似乎就只剩保存成本。O’Toole对《独立宣言》原件的讨论，使这种计算难以继续。即使文字已难辨读，具体物品仍然能在人们面对过去时发挥作用。我需要解释的，因而还有为什么是这个原件、它曾经历什么，以及人们如何通过它建立与过去的联系。
translation_en: But an emphasis only on information could also make this understanding too narrow. I once asked why originals were still needed if their words had already been copied and circulated. Behind this question was a view of archives mainly as sources of content for researchers. Once the content had been copied, keeping the original seemed to mean only preservation costs. O’Toole’s discussion of the original Declaration of Independence made this calculation difficult to maintain. Even when its writing was hard to read, the physical object could still matter in people’s encounters with the past. I therefore also needed to explain why this particular original mattered, what it had experienced, and how people used it to establish a connection with the past.

source_zh: 这并没有让我得出“原件总比复制品更有价值”的结论。文字副本与物质原件可以支持不同的问题：前者可能使内容易于利用，后者的删改、笔迹和保存经历则可能留下其他线索。原件受到尊重的方式，本身也可以被研究。我原先想用剩余信息量决定是否值得保存，现在则更愿意先明确，自己希望通过它认识什么。这种变化也与对档案员的理解相接：保存者需要辨认材料的不同关系，而不能只把它当作可以替换的信息容器。
translation_en: This did not lead me to conclude that “originals are always more valuable than copies.” A textual copy and a physical original can support different questions. The former may make content easier to use; alterations, handwriting, and the preservation history of the latter may offer other clues. How an original is respected can itself be studied. I used to want to decide whether something was worth preserving through the amount of information it still contained. I now prefer first to clarify what I hope to understand through it. This change also connects to my view of archivists: keepers need to recognize different relationships in materials rather than treating them as replaceable containers of information.

source_zh: 东德秘密警察档案又让我看到，保存与珍爱也不能直接相等。人们可以憎恶文件所代表的过去，同时又希望保留它们以追究责任。它们成为档案，并不表示保存者认同原来的用途；恰恰相反，后来使用可能改变记录与社会的关系。如果只按人们愿意纪念什么来理解档案，我就难以说明这种留存。档案能够支持的记忆未必令人自豪，使用它的人也不必拥有相同的感情。这使我更能理解，认定档案时需要考察具体联系，而不能预设一种统一的保存动机。
translation_en: The East German secret police archives also showed me that preservation cannot simply be equated with affection. People may hate the past that documents represent while wanting to keep them to hold people accountable. The fact that they become archives does not mean that their keepers approve of their original uses. Later use may instead change the relationship between records and society. If I understood archives only through what people wished to commemorate, I would struggle to explain this survival. The memories archives support need not inspire pride, and users need not share the same feelings. This helped me understand why identifying archives requires examining specific relationships rather than assuming a single motive for preservation.

source_zh: 相似的问题也出现在私存禁书与官方秘密档案之中。一份材料可以处在国家保管之下，却不符合公开叙事；它能够留存，也未必能够被普遍阅读。读Bartlett以后，我更难以按保管者的身份，直接决定一批材料代表谁的记忆。它为什么存在于这里，保存与使用分别受到什么限制，比先把它归入官方或民间更能帮助理解。这也使我修正“进入档案馆才成为档案”的直觉：机构位置很重要，但仍不足以代替对记录经历的认识。
translation_en: Similar questions appear in the secret preservation of banned books and in secret official archives. Materials can be in state custody without fitting the public narrative. They can survive without being widely accessible. After reading Bartlett, I find it harder to decide whose memory a collection represents simply from the identity of its keeper. Why it exists there, and what limits apply separately to preservation and use, help me understand it more than first classifying it as official or nonofficial. This also made me revise the intuition that materials become archives only after entering an archival institution. Institutional location matters, but it cannot replace an understanding of what records have gone through.

source_zh: 另一方面，承认选择和使用会改变意义，并不是说研究者可以任意把所有东西改称档案。住所帮助解释文件形成的条件，却不能仅凭这样的作用，就被用来证明任何一种经历；衣着能够呈现认同的尝试，也不直接说明每个人的内在信念。我现在更愿意保留这种区分。一个对象可以有遗产或纪念价值，也可以在特定问题下作为记录被研究，但几种用途需要分别说明。档案范围扩大之后，档案员与使用者都更需要交代自己在建立什么联系。
translation_en: At the same time, recognizing that selection and use change meaning does not allow researchers to call everything archives at will. A home can help explain the conditions in which documents were formed, but this role alone cannot make it evidence for any experience. Clothing can show attempts to express identity without directly revealing everyone’s inner beliefs. I now prefer to keep these distinctions. An object may have heritage or commemorative value and may also be studied as a record in relation to a particular question, but these uses need separate explanation. As the range of archives expands, both archivists and users need to make clearer which connections they are establishing.

source_zh: 还有一些联系，使我无法只从研究者的需要出发理解保存。那份要求阅后焚毁却仍被留下的文件，既提供了后来可以研究的痕迹，也保留了当时对保密的要求。我无法只凭它的存续确定命令如何执行，更不愿因为今天可以使用它，就反过来认为当事人理应保存一切。档案的形成涉及选择，也涉及记录者当下的处境。保存、开放与使用因而可能有不同条件；认识一种材料是什么，还需要理解它为什么被要求以特定方式对待。（Lee，第44—45页）
translation_en: Some connections also prevent me from understanding preservation only through researchers’ needs. The document ordered to be burned after reading, yet still preserved, offers a trace for later study while also retaining the demand for secrecy at the time. Its survival alone cannot tell me how the order was carried out. Nor would I assume that the people involved should have preserved everything simply because we can use it today. The formation of archives involves choices and the circumstances of those who created records. Preservation, access, and use may therefore require different conditions. Understanding what a material is also requires knowing why it was supposed to be treated in a particular way.

source_zh: 对“什么是档案”的重新思考，最终使我更谨慎，也更愿意学习具体对象。我不再只靠载体或保管地点作判断，也不认为共同的情感意义能够解释全部材料。记录与活动的联系、保存和描述的过程，以及后来能够提出的问题，都需要放在一起考虑。这样的理解仍然有待在不同材料中检验，却已改变了我的职业认识：档案员所面对的对象不是一份意义已经确定的清单。理解它们为什么成为档案，本身就是这份工作持续需要的研究。
translation_en: Rethinking “what are archives?” has ultimately made me more cautious and more willing to learn about particular objects. I no longer judge only by medium or place of custody, nor do I think a shared emotional meaning explains all materials. Connections between records and activities, processes of preservation and description, and the questions that can later be asked all need to be considered together. This understanding still needs to be tested against different materials, but it has already changed my view of the profession. Archivists do not work with a list of items whose meanings have already been settled. Understanding why they become archives is itself research that the profession continually requires.

source_zh: 结语
translation_en: Conclusion

source_zh: 回到最初的疑问，我现在更能说明档案员为什么需要理解材料。他们所要认识的，不只是文件说了什么，还包括记录怎样形成、为什么被保存，以及怎样使不同的人能够使用。我的变化，在于原来只从使用者的需要评价这份职业，现在开始尝试从工作的内部理解其中的判断。我也不再把伙伴关系寄托于档案员充分掌握每项研究，而是愿意学习对方的知识，并思考自己的提问如何才能进入交流。这是我在这几周中逐渐形成、也还需要继续实践的认识。
translation_en: Returning to my initial questions, I can now better explain why archivists need to understand materials. They need to know not only what documents say, but also how records were formed, why they were preserved, and how different people can use them. My change lies in moving from judging the profession only through users’ needs toward trying to understand its judgments from within the work. I no longer expect partnership to depend on archivists fully mastering every study. Instead, I am willing to learn from their knowledge and consider how my questions can become part of an exchange. This is an understanding I have gradually developed during these weeks and still need to put into practice.

source_zh: 因此，档案员成为历史研究者可以考虑的另一种职业方向，对我已经有了具体意义。历史训练可以用于解释一段过去，也可以用于研究和照顾使这种解释成为可能的材料。后一种工作需要专业方法、沟通能力和对判断后果的认识。理解这些要求之后，我才能认真看待职业的可能，而不只是觉得它同样与历史有关。今后使用档案时，我希望把这种认识落实为更好的提问，也让支持自己研究的劳动与知识进入论证。
translation_en: The possibility of archival work as another career direction for historical researchers therefore has a concrete meaning for me. Historical training can be used to interpret part of the past. It can also be used to study and care for the materials that make such interpretation possible. The latter work requires professional methods, communication skills, and an understanding of the consequences of judgment. Recognizing these demands allows me to consider the career seriously, rather than simply thinking that it also concerns history. When I use archives in the future, I hope to turn this understanding into better questions and to acknowledge in my arguments the work and knowledge supporting my research.

source_zh: “什么是档案”则使这份职业认识继续展开。我现在更愿意从记录与活动的关系出发，把物品怎样被留下、怎样被说明和使用纳入理解。档案员的作用与档案的范围因此彼此联系：对象的变化要求新的理解，专业判断又影响后来者怎样认识对象。我仍不能给所有材料一个没有例外的答案，但已经知道应该追问哪些关系。对我而言，思考的推进正在于，那个原来只负责保管文件的人，逐渐成为需要理解历史、也帮助他人理解历史的专业者。
translation_en: The question “what are archives?” extends this understanding of the profession. I now prefer to begin with relationships between records and activities, including how objects survive and how they are described and used. Archivists’ roles and the scope of archives are therefore connected: changing objects require new understandings, while professional judgments shape how later people understand those objects. I still cannot give a single answer that applies to every kind of material without exception, but I now know which relationships to ask about. For me, this is where my thinking has moved forward: the person I once saw as only keeping documents has gradually become a professional who needs to understand history and helps others understand it too.
